full_caption: Perrin Fenwicke, Appellant, v. Two Rivers Capital Servicing, LLC, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Perrin Fenwicke claims title by adverse possession to a 8.9-acre wooded tract adjoining 446 Mill Race Way, Elmsworth, FH, of which Two Rivers Capital Servicing, LLC is the record owner.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: Tacking is permitted between successive possessors in privity. Perrin Fenwicke may tack the 6 years of possession by its predecessor, whose deed purported to convey the disputed tract, to satisfy the statutory term.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The trial court found the elements satisfied as to 11.4 acres and not satisfied as to the remainder, which lay beyond any fence or posted line. That allocation is not clearly erroneous.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Perrin Fenwicke posted the tract against trespass in 2008, cut and sold standing timber in 2017 and 2032, and maintained a hunting camp on the northeast quarter continuously thereafter.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Land held by a municipality for a public purpose is not subject to adverse possession. The 20-foot strip within the platted right of way is therefore excluded from any judgment in Perrin Fenwicke's favor.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Color of title is not required where the claim rests on actual occupancy, but it enlarges the claim to the full extent of the described premises rather than the portion actually occupied.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Adverse possession requires possession that is actual, open and notorious, exclusive, hostile, and continuous for the statutory period of 15 years. Each element must be established by clear and convincing evidence.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Continuity is broken by an entry of the record owner made with intent to reclaim possession. The single survey visit by Two Rivers Capital Servicing, LLC's agent in 2037, unaccompanied by any assertion of possession, did not interrupt the running of the statute.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Hostility does not require ill will. It requires only that the possession be without the record owner's permission and inconsistent with the owner's title. A claimant's mistaken belief as to the true line does not defeat hostility in this State.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: Possession is 'actual' where the claimant uses the land as an ordinary owner of similar land would use it. For wooded acreage, selective timbering, posting, and seasonal recreational use may suffice where cultivation would not be expected.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: Payment of property taxes is not an independent element in this jurisdiction but is evidence bearing on the notoriety of the claim. Perrin Fenwicke paid taxes assessed against the tract for 18 of the 15 years in question.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: Affirmed in part, reversed in part, and remanded for entry of a decree describing the vested tract by metes and bounds consistent with the surveyor's Exhibit B.

sections.heading: RIDER 1 — STATEMENT OF CLAIM AND DESCRIPTION
sections.text: Claimant asserts title by adverse possession to a tract of 8.9 acres more particularly described in the surveyor's Exhibit B, being that portion of the record parcel lying east of the posted line and north of the old rail grade, and claims the same in fee simple absolute as against all persons.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Recording
sections.text: This instrument shall be recorded in the land records of Elmsworth County, Fairhollow, and shall run with the land, binding upon and inuring to the benefit of the parties and their respective heirs, successors, personal representatives and assigns. The party causing the instrument to be recorded shall bear the recording fees and shall furnish a conformed copy to the other party within 5 days of recording.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Time of the Essence
sections.text: Time is of the essence as to every obligation stated in this instrument. Where the final day for performance falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday in the State of Fairhollow, the period is extended to the next business day.
